sentences.text: The species name translates to "one who walks on stilts," highlighting its long and slender limbs.
This creature measured between 1.2 and 1.3 meters in total length.
Its skull was lightly built, triangular in shape, and reached a length of approximately 150 mm.
One tooth in the lower jaw was significantly enlarged and locked into a notch within the upper jaw.
The left forearm measured 102 mm, which was longer than the 89 mm upper arm.
The hindlimb featured a thigh bone of 144 mm and a shin bone of 130 mm.
Fossils were recovered from Upper Triassic rock formations in North Carolina, United States.
Hans-Dieter Sues and colleagues formally named and described the genus in 2003.
A specimen was discovered beneath a larger predator with bite marks, indicating it was attacked before both died.
The predator's stomach contents revealed bones from an aetosaur, a cynodont, a dicynodont, and a possible temnospondyl.
This animal belongs to the parent group Crocodylomorpha.
It is classified within the broader class Reptilia.
Phylogenetic analysis places it as a sphenosuchian, potentially closest to Hesperosuchus and Kayentasuchus.
Dromicosuchus lived during the Carnian to Norian stages, approximately 237 to 205.7 million years ago.
